items.title: Shields badge URL breaks when release-version contains "js-v" / "rust-v" prefix
items.body:
## Summary

`scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` only strips a single leading `v` before interpolating the release version into a shields.io `/badge/<label>-<message>-<color>` URL. When the caller passes a language-prefixed tag such as `js-v1.7.12` or `rust-v0.3.4`, the resulting URL contains extra unescaped `-` separators and shields.io returns the SVG `404: badge not found`.

This template works correctly for consumers that use a plain `v<version>` tag, but any downstream repo that multiplexes JS and Rust releases under `js-v<version>` / `rust-v<version>` tags hits the bug. For concrete evidence see [link-assistant/web-capture#98](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/98) and the [fix PR link-assistant/web-capture#99](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/99).

## Reproduction

```bash
curl -sS 'https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-js-v1.7.12-blue.svg' | head -c 200
```

Returns an SVG whose `aria-label="404: badge not found"`. The working form is:

```bash
curl -sS 'https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-1.7.12-blue.svg' | head -c 200
```

Which returns `aria-label="npm: 1.7.12"`.

## Offending line

`scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`:

```js
const versionWithoutV = version.replace(/^v/, '');
```

`version.replace(/^v/, '')` strips a leading single `v`. Given `js-v1.7.12`, `versionWithoutV` stays `js-v1.7.12`, and the next line interpolates it into a URL with four `-`-separated fields instead of the three that shields.io parses.

## Suggested fix

Pick one of the following. All are backward-compatible with consumers that pass a plain `v<version>`:

1. **Normalize the passed string** (what link-assistant/web-capture#99 ships):

   ```js
   const versionWithoutV = version
     .replace(/^[a-z]+-/i, '')   // drop "js-", "rust-", etc.
     .replace(/^v/i, '');        // drop leading "v"
   ```

2. **Use the dynamic shields endpoint** so the badge reads the current npm version directly and does not depend on the tag string:

   ```js
   const npmBadge = `[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/${PACKAGE_NAME}?label=npm&color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/${PACKAGE_NAME})`;
   ```

3. **Encourage callers to pass the clean numeric version** from `steps.publish.outputs.published_version` rather than the tag. `scripts/format-github-release.mjs` currently passes the full tag - it could strip the prefix at the call site instead.

## Workaround for affected downstreams

Until upstream fixes this, downstream consumers can override the version normalization as in link-assistant/web-capture@7ee8fe6 and optionally run a one-shot repair like [link-assistant/web-capture's fix-existing-release-badges.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/main/scripts/fix-existing-release-badges.mjs) against already-published releases.

## Related

- Rust pipeline template sidesteps the issue because it uses `/crates/v/<name>` (dynamic) rather than `/badge/...` (static).
- shields.io /badge syntax reference: https://shields.io/badges/static-badge

items.title: fix: normalize release badge versions for prefixed tags
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #40.

This PR fixes the release-note npm badge formatter for prefixed release tags such as `js-v1.7.12` and `rust-v0.3.4`. The formatter now extracts the semantic version before building the npm badge, escapes shields.io static badge message separators, and keeps links pointed at the exact npm package version.

## What Changed

- Added `scripts/format-release-notes-helpers.mjs` for release-version normalization and shields.io static badge path escaping.
- Updated `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` to use the helper instead of `version.replace(/^v/, '')`.
- Added regression tests for plain `v`, `js-v`, `rust-v`, and prefixed prerelease tags.
- Added a patch changeset.
- Added `docs/case-studies/issue-40/` with issue/PR data, CI logs, live shields.io SVG evidence, downstream web-capture evidence, Rust-template snapshots, and CI/CD comparison notes.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, this shields.io URL returns a `404: badge not found` SVG:

```sh
curl -sS 'https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-js-v1.7.12-blue.svg' | head -c 200
```

The normalized form returns `npm: 1.7.12`:

```sh
curl -sS 'https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-1.7.12-blue.svg' | head -c 200
```

## Verification

- `node --test tests/release-badge.test.js`
- `npm test`
- `npm run check`
- `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- `npx --yes -p secretlint -p @secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend secretlint "**/*"`

## Rust Template Check

The Rust template was checked at `353d89396fd420339f2dab0e548ca2caf6198cd5`. It uses dynamic `img.shields.io/crates/v/<crate>` badges instead of static `/badge/<label>-<message>-<color>` npm badges, so this exact issue was not present there and no Rust-template issue was filed.

items.title: Support multi-language monorepos: auto-detect layout, namespace release tags/titles, badge the artifact
items.body:
## Support multi-language monorepos: auto-detect layout, namespace releases, and badge the artifact

When a repository hosts more than one language (e.g. `js/` + `rust/` in one monorepo, each driven by its template's release workflow), the per-language releases collide in a single flat namespace and the GitHub release does not link to the artifact it published. Discovered while shipping [link-assistant/web-search#15](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/15); full write-up in [PR #16](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/pull/16) (`docs/case-studies/issue-15`).

### Request

Make the release job adapt with **no configuration**:

1. **Auto-detect layout.** Manifest at the repo root → single-language; manifest in a language subdirectory (`js/package.json`, `js/package.json`, `rust/Cargo.toml`, …) → multi-language.
   ```bash
   if [ -f package.json ]; then ROOT=.; MULTI=false; else ROOT=js; MULTI=true; fi
   ```
2. **Namespace the tag** in multi-language mode: `js_v<version>` (keep a plain `v<version>` single-language).
3. **Prefix the release title** `[JavaScript] <version>` in multi-language mode (`<name> <version>` single-language).
4. **Badge the published artifact** in the release body — a shields.io badge linking to the exact version page: `https://www.npmjs.com/package/<pkg>/v/<version>`. Build the link from the **bare** version (strip any `v`/`lang_v` prefix first) so it resolves to the version page rather than 404ing.

A small, unit-tested helper keeps tag/title construction **idempotent** (re-running on an already-prefixed version must not double-prefix).

### Reference implementation

`js/scripts/release-naming.mjs` (+ `release-naming.test.js`, 21 cases) and the `version` step of `.github/workflows/rust.yml` in [link-assistant/web-search#16](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/pull/16).

items.title: Fix: Support Major/Minor/Patch changes in release formatting script
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #3 - The release formatting script now correctly handles all changeset types (Major, Minor, Patch) instead of only Patch changes.

## Problem

The `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` script only handled `### Patch Changes` sections, causing it to fail on Minor and Major releases:
- ❌ Section headers remained in release notes
- ❌ PR detection was skipped
- ❌ Release formatting failed silently

**Example:** Release v0.1.0 showed:
```markdown
### Minor Changes

- 65d76dc: Initial template setup...
```

## Solution

Updated the regex pattern to match all changeset types:
- Replace hardcoded "Patch Changes" with flexible `(Major|Minor|Patch) Changes` pattern
- Extract commit hash from both inline and embedded formats
- Add informative logging for debugging

**After fix**, releases will show clean formatting:
```markdown
Initial template setup...

**Related Pull Request:** #X

---

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-0.1.0-blue.svg)](...)
```

## Implementation

### Core Changes
- **scripts/format-release-notes.mjs** (lines 92-122):
  - New flexible regex pattern matching all changeset types
  - Handles optional commit hash formats
  - Improved error messages

### Testing
Created comprehensive test suite in `experiments/`:
- ✅ `test-format-major-changes.mjs` - Tests Major changes
- ✅ `test-format-minor-changes.mjs` - Tests Minor changes
- ✅ `test-format-patch-changes.mjs` - Tests Patch changes
- ✅ `test-format-no-hash.mjs` - Tests without commit hash

All tests passing ✅

### Documentation
- **docs/case-studies/issue-3/README.md** - Comprehensive case study:
  - Timeline of events
  - Root cause analysis
  - Impact assessment
  - Solution design

## Related Work

**Issues created in affected repositories:**
- link-foundation/gh-download-pull-request#5
- link-foundation/gh-download-issue#5
- link-foundation/test-anywhere (creation attempted)

**Reference implementation:**
- link-assistant/agent#59 (original fix)
- link-assistant/agent#58 (original issue)

## Testing

✅ Local CI checks passing:
- ESLint
- Prettier
- File size checks

✅ GitHub Actions CI passing
✅ All unit tests passing

## Verification

To verify the fix works:
1. Run test scripts: `npm test`
2. Check Major changes: `node experiments/test-format-major-changes.mjs`
3. Check Minor changes: `node experiments/test-format-minor-changes.mjs`
4. Check Patch changes: `node experiments/test-format-patch-changes.mjs`

## Impact

- **Low risk** - Backward compatible with existing Patch changes
- **High value** - Enables proper formatting for all release types
- **Well tested** - Comprehensive test coverage
- **Documented** - Full case study in docs/

---
